prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
Done. The game is at `game/index.html`, single file, no build step.

**[goal]** A Win95-era archery game, level 1: mouse aim, hold-to-draw power, balloons to pop, on-screen score, start and lose conditions, good feel and sound.

**[action]** Wrote `game/index.html` (HTML+CSS+canvas+Web Audio, only external resource is Google Fonts "Press Start 2P"), then verified live in a browser: start screen → START → balloons spawning and rising → 3 escapes → GAME OVER overlay → TRY AGAIN restart. Closed all browser tabs afterwards.

**[result]** How it plays:
- **Aim**: bow points at the cursor. **Draw**: hold the mouse button — power ramps 0→100 in under a second (on-screen power bar + rising creak, string and nocked arrow visibly pull back, dotted trajectory preview). **Shoot**: release — twang + whoosh, arrow flies with gravity; weak shots fall short, so power is a real decision.
- **Balloons**: pop up from below, 6 colors, wobble, +10 each with particle burst, screen shake and a pitched pop sound.
- **Win**: reach 100 points → "LEVEL 1 COMPLETE!" with a jingle. **Lose**: let 3 balloons escape (lives ♥♥♥ in the Win95 HUD) → red flash, sad tone, "GAME OVER" with score and retry.
- **Look**: teal desktop, gray window chrome with navy title bar, beveled panels and buttons, pixel font, sun, drifting clouds, grass.

**[assumptions I made (no second turn allowed)]** Win = 100 pts; lose = 3 escapes; arrows unlimited but power-gated by range; mouse-only (no touch); sound synthesized with Web Audio so no asset files are needed; audio starts on the first click to satisfy autoplay policy.

**[evidence]** Screenshots confirmed: start screen rendered; live play with balloons rising; GAME OVER appeared after 3 balloons escaped (lives shown ♡♡♡) while I was mid-check; `TRY AGAIN` click returned "restarted" and the overlay hid; no JS exceptions surfaced (page loop kept running; the one exec error was my own variable-name collision in the test snippet, not the page). One caveat: I didn't land a verified pop-on-hit in-browser (balloon positions are random and the sim shot fired at a weak power), but the collision code path is the same one that ran without error during the simulated shot.
